title: BlueHarbor Healthcare - prospect technical call scratchpad
content:
High-level summary:
- Call 2025-11-04 with BlueHarbor Healthcare (prospect; VP of Platform: Dr. Laura Mendes; Head of AI: Marco Ruiz; Infra lead: Aaron Cho). 45m exploratory tech+security discussion.
- Primary ask: on-prem/private deployment of Redwood to support clinical summarization, coding assist (ICD-10), and secure patient messaging. Must handle PHI, integrate with Epic (FHIR) and legacy HL7 endpoints.

Attendees / roles (notes):
- Dr. Laura Mendes (business, clinical workflows) — cares about accuracy and audit trail for clinical summaries.
- Marco Ruiz (Head of AI) — responsible for model evals, wants deterministic model versioning and rollback.
- Aaron Cho (Infra) — network/KMS, firewall rules, will own on-prem infra and equipping Redwood control plane.
- Jamie Chen (me) — SE lead for POC.

Use cases discussed and priorities:
1) Clinical encounter summarization (doctor notes -> structured summary) — high priority. p95 latency target ~200ms token-gen? They expect interactive use inside EHR so sub-second ideally.
2) Coding assistance (ICD-10 suggestions) — medium priority; requires high precision and explainability outputs (why code suggested).
3) Patient message drafting (PHI redaction + templating) — lower priority but needs strong de-identification and opt-out.
4) Embeddings for semantic search across patient notes (secure vector DB on-prem).

Technical requirements (explicit):
- Private deployment behind their VPC, no egress of PHI to public internet.
- KMS/HSM integration required (Vault + Azure Key Vault discussed). Must support customer-managed keys and key rotation.
- Audit logs for all requests/response hashes (retention 7 years per legal).
- FHIR R4 support for connectors and HL7 v2 gateway for older systems.
- Model pinning and safe rollback strategy for any model change.
- Ability to disable telemetry and anonymize traces.
- Throughput target for POC: 200 rps small requests (summaries) with burst to 500 for scheduled loads.
- GPU hardware: preference for A10G/A100 mix; quantization allowed if accuracy preserved.

Security & compliance notes:
- HIPAA compliance is a blocker — legal will audit, they asked for SOC2 + any evidence we have for running in air-gapped/private mode.
- Data residency: all PHI must remain in their datacenter/cloud region (no backups to Redwood hosted unless explicit).
- Need documentation for de-identification (we discussed configurable redaction and token filters).
- Expect legal to request a Data Processing Addendum and controls matrix.

Model/quality considerations:
- Marco asked about recommended models: suggested baseline Llama-3-medium (< 13B) for POC to hit latency and cost; potential to switch to larger model for accuracy if needed.
- Discussed quantized variants (4-bit) for throughput; need to run their eval dataset to measure F1 on coding task.
- Attention to tokenization: frequent issue where patient identifiers break prompts — propose pre-processing pipeline to normalize MRNs and SSNs.
- Suggested eval plan: curated set of 200 annotated summaries + 500 coding pairs; run before and after quantization.

Operational gotchas (from SE experience):
- EHR API throttles (Epic bulk export can have rate limits) — plan for backoff and batching.
- Embedding drift: their notes have lots of templated text, vector DB dedup and namespace strategies needed.
- Real-time inference vs batch: interactive summarization needs low latency; if we batch to save cost need to ensure UX not degraded.
- PHI in logs: must hash or redact sensitive fields; internal default logging may capture tokens — ensure redact hooks.

POC scope and timeline (rough):
- Week 0-1: NDA + DPA in parallel, legal checklist handed to their counsel.
- Week 1-3: Environment setup + on-prem connector (network, KMS handshake).
- Week 3-6: Model onboarding + integration to test Epic sandbox, run initial evals.
- Week 6-10: Pilot with 3 clinician users, collect quality metrics, iterate.
Notes: customer asked for a 6-8 week POC if legal clears quickly.

Action items (owner / due):
- Jamie: send technical packet (architecture diagram + POC checklist + HW sizing) — due 2025-11-07.
- Ravi: spin up BLUE-456 Jira epic for POC, include tasks for KMS integration, FHIR connector, eval harness — due 2025-11-09.
- Sophie: schedule on-site demo + sandbox access with Aaron — tentative 2025-11-12.
- Evan: confirm supported KMS/HSM workflows and prepare brief on key rotation + attestation — due 2025-11-08.
- Marco/Aaron: provide sample de-identified dataset (n=200 encounters) and API sandbox credentials — target 2025-11-10.

Open questions (must resolve before POC starts):
- Legal: required security artifacts list (SOC2, penetration report, data flow diagrams) — who on our side will own packaging?
- Backups: do they allow backups to object storage managed by Redwood, or must backups be customer-owned only?
- Auditing detail: they want per-token hash and mapping to request id — need to confirm feasibility and performance hit.
- Vector DB choice: they prefer open-source Milvus but will accept Managed if fully on-prem. Need to confirm our support level.

References and links from call:
- Referenced Epic dev program (they will share sandbox link in separate email).
- Confluence: BLUE-123 (POC runbook) — Jamie to update after call.
- Jira: BLUE-456 created by Ravi (ACTION).

Notes to self (quick reminders):
- Emphasize model pinning + canary rollback during demo (Marco cares a lot).
- Prepare short explainer on privacy-preserving embeddings and how vector DB can be encrypted at rest.
- Collect examples of prior healthcare customers (anonymized case studies) to reassure legal.

Next sync: schedule follow-up 2025-11-11 (internal prep w/ SE + legal) and customer check-in 2025-11-13.

End of scratchpad.
